content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High paging activity + model warmup failures on serving cluster us-west-2. P50 latency for /v1/generate embeddings spiked 3x. Auto-eviction and container restarts observed. Pages: https://internal/alerts/4995004321
ash (oncall): I'm on it, looking at the warmup logs now.
maria (eng-sre): seeing repeated CUDA OOMs during model deserialize on node g-45 and g-46, pods restarting in ~30s intervals. stack snippet attached in logs.
marta (runtime): throwaway note: warmup path uses full KV cache allocation which compounds paging on heavy-concurrent warmups.
ash (oncall): can we throttle warmup concurrency? any quick config to reduce parallel preloads?
marta (runtime): yes — we can set runtime.warmup.max_concurrent_load=1 per node via configmap. That will slow new activations but stop stampede. Recommend immediate patch.
devops-bot: autoscaler triggered additional node add 3 -> 6 (scale_up). However scale_up landed mixed GPU SKUs; some are smaller VMs causing more paging.
prod-metrics-bot: metric spike: disk swap in pages/sec up 8x on g-4x nodes, GPU mem alloc failures increased 200%.
sam (cust-suc): I’m pulling list of active customer sessions hitting embeddings-route. Early check: two enterprise customers (acme-inc, finlytics) reported degraded requests. Reached out to account leads.
maria (eng-sre): logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T12:05:21Z ERROR runtime: model-warmup failed: DeserializationError: unexpected EOF while reading tensor bytes
2026-03-14T12:05:22Z ERROR runtime: cuda: runtime error: out of memory (cudaMalloc) at allocate.cpp:142
2026-03-14T12:05:22Z ERROR runtime: kernel compile timeout: CompileTimeoutError: nvrtc compile exceeded 30s
2026-03-14T12:05:23Z WARN node-manager: container crash detected, restarting pod redwood-worker-ggg on g-45
```
ash (oncall): compile timeout + OOM + deser errors — smells like two simultaneous problems: 1) hot nodes running many warmups causing paging (OOM); 2) corruption or truncated artifact on one shard giving deserialization EOF.
marta (runtime): agree. For immediate mitigation: 1) patch configmap to limit warmup concurrency to 1 and disable prefetch for embeddings model v2; 2) mark suspect shard as quarantined to avoid loading until we verify artifact integrity; 3) enable fallback routing to v1-small model for new requests.
ash (oncall): executing step 1 now -> kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-config
data:
  WARMUP_MAX_CONCURRENT_LOAD: "1"
  WARMUP_PREFETCH: "false"
EOF

kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redwood-worker

nash (oncall): applied and restarting workers. Rolling restart in progress — expect reduced throughput but should stop new simultaneous warmups.
prod-metrics-bot: after config change: paging rate down 45% within 90s, OOM errors decreased but node g-45 still experiencing crashes.
maria (eng-sre): investigating node g-45 artifact: checksum mismatch during fetch for shard s-12. I'm pulling the artifact store logs.
marta (runtime): to be safe, add route fallback in router config: route embeddings.v2 -> embeddings.v1-small with header X-incident-fallback for new traffic. That avoids capacity-heavy model for existing customers.
sam (cust-suc): pushing message to impacted customers: "We're seeing degraded performance on embeddings in us-west-2 due to backend warmup/paging issues. We're routing new requests to a smaller model and expect reduced latency within ~15-30 minutes. We'll update when fully mitigated."
devops-bot: quarantine action taken: node g-45 isolated from scheduler (cordon + drain) to prevent further restarts while SRE inspects disk and mounts.
maria (eng-sre): artifact logs show partial download then abrupt connection reset from artifact-proxy 10.42.0.9, correlates with network flapping on g-45. Running md5sum on local copy shows mismatch.
nash (oncall): next steps planned: 1) keep warmup throttled; 2) quaratine node g-45 until artifact re-sync; 3) route traffic to v1-small for enterprise customers; 4) schedule manual artifact re-sync for s-12; 5) monitor latency and error budget.
jia (next-oncall): I’ll take first responder after ash; prepping handoff in 10m. Please include any open runbook steps.
marta (runtime): runbook snippet for future: if you see compile timeout + OOM on warmup -> reduce warmup concurrency, disable prefetch, toggle quantization-friendly path (runtime.quantize.fast_load=true) and quarantine node.
maria (eng-sre): artifact re-sync started from S3 copy, verifying checksum now. If re-sync succeeds we'll unquarantine node and re-introduce with warmup disabled initially.
sam (cust-suc): update to customers sent. Two customers asked for ETA and asked to be routed to a dedicated cluster; sales contact info provided.
prod-metrics-bot: after fallback routing in place: P50 returned to 1.2x baseline, errors dropped to within SLA for all but quarantined node.
nash (oncall): summary for postmortem prep: root causes likely: (A) warmup stampede interacting with limited GPU memory causing paging and OOMs, amplified by mixed-sku autoscale; (B) artifact partial download caused deserialization EOF and repeated retries on same node; (C) kernel compile timeouts secondary to heavy CPU contention while swapping. Mitigations applied: throttle warmup concurrency, quarantine node, fallback routing, manual artifact re-sync.
jia (next-oncall): taking over monitoring. Ash — handoff notes?
nash (oncall): handoff: keep warmup concurrency=1 until we roll a stable artifact; verify md5 for s-12, keep node cordoned until cleaned; watch P50 and error rate for embeddings route for 2 hours. Contact marta if compile timeouts reappear.
jia (next-oncall): acknowledged. Escalation: if error rate > 2% for 10m, call paging-sig channel and consider temporary regional rate limit.
maria (eng-sre): unquarantine plan: after artifact verified and node rebooted with warmup disabled, run a controlled warmup of single shard and monitor memory/paging for 10m before full traffic.
sam (cust-suc): will follow up with customers with status update in 30m.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV-2. Tags: paging, warmup, artifact-corrupt, cuda-oom. Incident created: #INC-2026-4995004321
ash (oncall): closing thread for now — monitoring. Will open postmortem doc once incident is stable. Thanks team. :heart:
